scope: Offline first-seen point-reuse hypothesis against six pinned native output vertex sets; not native execution or a production algorithm
method: Seed a simple list with unique Float32 source vertices. Visit precise experimental-collector endpoints in face/hit order, reuse an existing point within the inferred conditional radius, otherwise insert the endpoint rounded to Float32. Compare distinct model points with distinct native output vertices.
interpretation: This simple first-seen model reproduces the rotated and wide-above vertex sets but leaves extra points in the other four controls. It is not a complete explanation for native behavior and is not suitable as a generic merge rule.
limitations: Collector order and initial tree membership are hypotheses, not observed native state.
Only vertex sets are compared; no triangulation, ownership, GUI/MCP or native parity claim follows.
The native controls omit some real geometry, so a distance rule must not be adopted merely to fit these outputs.
